description.title: The universal operator set U of the Selling closure
description.reference: P. H. Zwart, The Selling closure: a complete operator set for reindexing, and the price of pseudo-symmetry (Acta Cryst. A), Section 3.3 and Appendix A
description.contents: every unimodular integer matrix that carries one obtuse (Selling-reduced) superbase of a lattice to another obtuse superbase of the same lattice, for any lattice; 6096 = 48 x 127 matrices with entries in {-3, ..., 3}, closed under inversion and under the 48 relabellings of a reduced superbase
description.reduced_basis: a Selling-reduced basis (a, b, c) is the last three vectors of an obtuse superbase (d, a, b, c), d = -a-b-c, all six pairwise dot products <= 0
description.W: W[n] is a 3 x 3 integer matrix given as a list of rows; column j of W[n] is the j-th new basis vector written in the old reduced basis (a, b, c)
description.det: det[n] is the determinant of W[n], +1 or -1; 3048 of each
description.usage: with B_R and B_N the reduced bases of a reference and a new cell (columns are basis vectors, in each cell's input basis), the candidate operators are P = B_R W B_N^-1, which satisfy G_N ~ s P^T G_R P for metric tensors G and a scale s; keep the W with det(W) = det(B_R) det(B_N) for proper P, price each candidate and keep those within the band. The list contains the true operator whenever the reference's widened set lies in the first layer (Remark A8).
